requirements.text: Native SwiftUI iOS app, 100% local, zero network calls, no accounts/sign-in/analytics/telemetry/crash SDKs, no backend of any kind.
All state (saved game, stats, settings) persists strictly on-device (FileManager/UserDefaults/SwiftData), no iCloud/CloudKit sync.

Fully correct single-deck Klondike rules engine: 7 tableau columns, 4 foundations, alternating-color descending tableau sequences, ascending same-suit foundation moves, King-only placement into empty tableau columns.

Tap-to-move interaction through one shared validation/mutation function: single legal destination auto-executes, multiple legal destinations highlight for a confirming tap, zero legal destinations shows blocked-move feedback.
Tap-based relocation of a validly-stacked tableau run (maximal face-up alternating-descending sequence) as a single atomic unit, via the same validation path as single-card moves.
No illegal move is ever able to mutate game state.
True win detection fires only when all 4 foundations are complete.

Explicit stuck-board (no-legal-move) detection, surfaced distinctly from a win, computed correctly for the active draw mode: draw-1 via the exact static pass, draw-3 via a documented conservative approximation biased toward not falsely declaring stuck.
Full multi-step undo with exact prior-state restoration (board, face-up flags, counters).
New Game / fresh deal requires explicit user confirmation whenever the current game is unfinished (not won, not stuck).
Stock/waste/foundation/tableau layout fully supporting both draw-1 and draw-3 modes, each with correct draw-count semantics and its own stuck-detection behavior.
Unlimited stock redeal/recycle, documented in-app wherever rules/help content appears.

Bespoke, original rank/suit card face system (not SF Symbols reused as suit glyphs) using a systematic/generative shared visual grammar across all 52 cards and the card back, legible at true on-device card width (~45-50pt) as a hard pass/fail gate.
Real card-stock texture, shadow, and lighting in card rendering.
Spring-based deal/flip animation with per-card sequencing and real card art, playing only on a genuinely fresh deal (first launch or explicit New Game), never replaying on a resumed cold launch.
Fully art-directed light and dark mode (not simple color inversion), implemented via one shared Theme token file with no literal colors/fonts elsewhere.
One clear, original signature visual/interaction hook identifiable from a single glance/screenshot.
Haptic feedback on move accepted, move rejected (if implemented), and win, verified by source inspection of the trigger call sites.

Stats screen showing games played, games won, best time, and streak, tracked separately per draw mode (draw-1 vs draw-3), never combined, with a real per-mode empty state before any game completes in that mode.
Best time displays 'N/A' when the timer is disabled, never a fabricated or stale value.

Settings screen with draw-1/draw-3 selection (switching mid-game requires the same confirmation pattern as New Game: confirm discards and re-deals in the new mode, cancel leaves setting and game untouched), card-back selection (applies live at any time), and timer on/off.
Game timer starts on the first state-mutating action (a confirmed move or stock draw), pauses when the app is backgrounded, and respects the timer-on/off setting.
Local, silent game-event recording (session start/end, elapsed seconds, undo count, outcome) begins from day one and feeds the Stats screen.

Persisted game state represents settled logical state only (piles, face-up flags), never in-flight animation position; writes are atomic (temp-then-swap) and survive backgrounding, force-quit, and relaunch without corruption.
No encryption layer for local persistence — plain FileManager/UserDefaults/SwiftData only.
Explicit VoiceOver labels per card (e.g. 'Seven of Hearts, tableau column 3, face up'), non-color-only suit differentiation, and Reduce Motion fallback for spring/flip/deal animations.
System LaunchScreen themed to the app's card-table background, not left as default white.
App is locked to portrait-only orientation at the project level.
App launches directly into the resumed active game or a fresh deal, with no interstitial start/menu screen.
Settings includes a disclosure line that stats/progress are device-local only and will be lost on reinstall or device migration.
No monetization surface of any kind (no IAP, ads, or subscriptions).
No multiplayer, social features, leaderboards, Game Center, or achievements.
Zero placeholder screens among Game, Stats, and Settings — every screen shows real, meaningful, non-fabricated content.
Win-screen native share sheet sharing a rendered image of the completed board with a solve-time caption.
Live interactive drag gestures (single-card and multi-card) as an alternative/addition to tap-to-move.
